memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Now Lot, who was moving about with Abram, also had flocks and herds and tents. But the land could not support them while they stayed together, for their possessions were so great that they were not able to stay together. And quarreling arose between Abram's herders and Lot's. The Canaanites and Perizzites were also living in the land at that time. - Gen 13:5-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is an unexpected problem: they had too much. The flocks were too many, the land too small, and so "quarreling arose." Prosperity, not poverty, is what divided this family. We usually expect hardship to strain relationships, but abundance can do it just as easily.

Wealth promises to solve our problems and often creates new ones. Abram and Lot had walked together through famine and journey, but they could not walk together through prosperity. The blessings we chase can become the very things that pull us apart.

Notice the painful detail at the end: "The Canaanites and Perizzites were also living in the land at that time." The neighbours were watching. God's people were squabbling in full view of those who did not know Him. Our conflicts are rarely private; a watching world sees how we handle disagreement, and it shapes what they think of our God.

Jesus said, "By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another" (John 13:35). How we treat one another in conflict is part of our witness. When abundance or difference threatens to divide us, remember who is watching - and remember that relationships are worth more than what we're arguing over.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Has prosperity ever caused more strain in your relationships than hardship?
- Who is watching how you handle conflict?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, keep my possessions from dividing me from people. Help me value relationships above things, and let a watching world see Your love in the way I handle conflict.
Amen.
